person.note: The human body is mostly organic molecules (C,H,O,N), calcium in bones, and iron in hemoglobin.

bicycle.note: Steel or aluminium frame, rubber tyres (C), chromium plating, copper brake cables.

car.note: Steel body (Fe), aluminium engine, copper wiring, silicon electronics, lead-acid battery.

motorcycle.note: Steel or aluminium frame, chrome surfaces, copper electrical system.

airplane.note: Aluminium fuselage, titanium and nickel in jet engines, carbon-fibre composites in modern aircraft.

bus.note: Heavy steel body, aluminium trim, copper wiring and motors.

train.note: Steel rails and body, aluminium cars (modern), copper motors and overhead wires.

truck.note: Heavy-gauge steel frame, aluminium cab panels, copper wiring, lead-acid battery.

boat.note: Aluminium or fibreglass (C/Si) hull, steel fittings, zinc sacrificial anodes prevent corrosion.

traffic light.note: Steel housing, aluminium visor, copper wiring, LEDs contain semiconductors and rare phosphors.

fire hydrant.note: Cast iron body, bronze (Cu+Sn) fittings and valve seats.

stop sign.note: Aluminium panel, retroreflective coating contains titanium dioxide and glass microspheres (Si).

parking meter.note: Aluminium or stainless steel housing, copper coins, silicon electronics.

bench.note: Iron or steel frame (urban benches), wooden slats are cellulose (C,H,O), sometimes aluminium.

bird.note: Organic biology: carbon-based tissues, calcium phosphate bones, iron in blood, silica in beak keratin.

cat.note: Mammalian biology: carbon-based tissues, calcium bones, iron-rich blood, trace minerals.

dog.note: Mammalian biology identical in composition to other vertebrates; iron in haemoglobin.

horse.note: Large mammal; keratin in hooves contains sulphur; calcium-rich bones support heavy weight.

sheep.note: Wool is keratin, rich in sulphur; biology otherwise typical mammalian composition.

cow.note: Mammalian biology; milk production requires extra calcium and phosphorus.

elephant.note: Tusks are calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite) with trace manganese giving ivory its colour.

bear.note: Large omnivore; dense calcium bones, high iron diet from fish and meat.

zebra.note: Black-and-white striping from melanin (C,H,N,O,S); standard mammalian biology otherwise.

giraffe.note: Tallest land animal; high blood pressure demands a large, calcium-dense skeleton.

backpack.note: Nylon or polyester (C,H,O,N) shell, aluminium frame stays, zinc or aluminium zippers.

umbrella.note: Steel or fibreglass ribs, polyester canopy (C,H,N,O), aluminium or steel shaft.

handbag.note: Leather or synthetic fabric; hardware (clasps, zippers) uses zinc alloys, gold or silver plating.

tie.note: Silk (natural protein, C/H/N/O/S) or polyester (synthetic polymer, C/H/O).

suitcase.note: Aluminium frame, polycarbonate or nylon shell (C,H,O,N), zinc alloy locks and wheels.

frisbee.note: Injection-moulded polyethylene or nylon — almost entirely carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.

skis.note: Carbon-fibre or fibreglass (C,Si) core, steel edges, aluminium or titanium reinforcements.

snowboard.note: Fibreglass/carbon layers, steel edges, polyethylene base — lightweight composites throughout.

sports ball.note: Vulcanised rubber (C,H,S) bladder, polyurethane or leather cover. Sulphur cross-links the rubber.

kite.note: Polyester or nylon sail (C,H,N,O), fibreglass or aluminium spars, polyester line.

baseball bat.note: Ash or maple wood (cellulose C/H/O) or aluminium alloy — both very lightweight materials.

baseball glove.note: Tanned leather (collagen C/H/O/N), chromium salts used in tanning, oil conditioner.

skateboard.note: Maple wood deck (C/H/O), aluminium trucks, steel axle and bearings.

surfboard.note: Polyurethane foam core (C,H,N,O), fibreglass (Si) skin, epoxy resin.

tennis racket.note: Graphite (C) or carbon-fibre frame, fibreglass (Si), titanium or aluminium reinforcement.

bottle.note: Soda-lime glass (Si,O,Na,Ca) or PET plastic (C,H,O). Glass historically contains lead as stabiliser.

wine glass.note: Soda-lime silicate glass; lead crystal contains PbO for sparkle and weight.

cup.note: Ceramic (Si/Al/O) or borosilicate glass; metal cups use stainless steel (Fe/Cr/Ni).

fork.note: Stainless steel (18% Cr, 8% Ni in 18-8 grade). Chromium gives corrosion resistance.

knife.note: Stainless or high-carbon steel blade; higher carbon increases hardness and edge retention.

spoon.note: 18-8 stainless steel identical to fork; chosen for non-reactivity with food.

bowl.note: Ceramic (porcelain or stoneware) is aluminium silicate; glazes add various metal oxides for colour.

banana.note: Bananas are famously high in potassium. The carbon-based sugars are the primary energy source.

apple.note: Mostly water and carbohydrates (C,H,O); potassium and trace minerals in skin and flesh.

sandwich.note: Bread (starch C/H/O), protein (N), salt (NaCl), calcium from cheese, iron from meat.

orange.note: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) plus flavonoids; citrus pigments contain carotenoids (C/H/O).

broccoli.note: Glucosinolates give broccoli its taste — sulphur-containing compounds (C/H/N/O/S).

carrot.note: Orange colour from beta-carotene (C/H), a precursor to Vitamin A. High potassium.

hot dog.note: Processed meat: protein (N), fat (C/H), sodium nitrite preservative, haem iron from muscle.

pizza.note: Flour (C/H/O starch), cheese (Ca, fat), tomato (K), salt (NaCl); silicon from wheat silica bodies.

donut.note: Deep-fried dough: sugars and fats (C/H/O), baking powder (Na), eggs (N/S).

cake.note: Flour, eggs, sugar, butter — all organic compounds with sodium from baking soda.

chair.note: Metal frame (Fe or Al), fabric or plastic seat (C/H/O/N). Wood chairs are cellulose.

couch.note: Foam (polyurethane C/H/O/N), fabric cover, steel spring core, aluminium or wood frame.

potted plant.note: Plant tissue (cellulose C/H/O), chlorophyll (Mg), clay pot (Si/Al/O), fertiliser minerals.

bed.note: Steel spring frame, wood slats (C/H/O), cotton or polyester mattress (C/H/O/N).

dining table.note: Steel or aluminium legs, wood or glass top; stainless or chrome finish.

toilet.note: Vitreous china (Si/Al/O/Ca glaze), chrome-plated brass fittings, copper supply pipes.

tv.note: Silicon LCD/OLED panel, indium tin oxide (ITO) electrodes, rare-earth phosphors in screen coating.

laptop.note: Silicon chips, aluminium chassis, lithium-ion battery, copper wiring, gold contacts, cobalt cathode.

mouse.note: Plastic shell (C/H/O/N), silicon sensor and electronics, copper traces, silver switch contacts.

remote.note: Plastic case (C/H/O), silicon IR sensor, silver contacts, zinc-carbon or alkaline batteries.

keyboard.note: Silicon membrane or mechanical switches, ABS plastic keys (C/H/N), copper PCB traces, silver contacts.

cell phone.note: Silicon SoC, aluminium/glass body, lithium battery, gold bond wires, cobalt cathode, tantalum capacitors.

microwave.note: Stainless steel cavity (Fe/Cr/Ni), aluminium trim, copper magnetron coils, silicon electronics.

oven.note: Stainless steel body (Fe/Cr/Ni), nickel heating elements, aluminium racks.

toaster.note: Nichrome (Ni/Cr) resistance wire heats the bread; stainless steel outer shell.

sink.note: Stainless steel bowl (Fe/Cr/Ni for 304-grade), or porcelain-enamelled cast iron, copper plumbing.

refrigerator.note: Steel outer cabinet, aluminium evaporator, copper refrigerant coils, HFCs (C/H/F) as refrigerant.

book.note: Cellulose paper (C/H/O), printing ink (C/H/O/N pigments), calcium carbonate filler, TiO₂ whitener.

clock.note: Steel or brass gears, silicon quartz crystal oscillator, copper coils, gold or silver plating.

vase.note: Soda-lime glass or ceramic; coloured glazes add metal oxides (Fe for amber, Cu for blue-green).

scissors.note: Stainless steel blades (Fe/Cr/Ni); high-carbon steel for sharper, harder edges.

teddy bear.note: Polyester or cotton fabric (C/H/O/N), polyester fiberfill, plastic eyes and nose.

hair drier.note: Nichrome (Ni/Cr) heating coil, copper motor windings, aluminium or plastic housing, silicon electronics.

toothbrush.note: Polypropylene handle (C/H), nylon bristles (C/H/N/O), titanium dioxide whitener in some bristles.
